integer_semantics: win and n are 16-bit signed ints; MSC arithmetic right shift (SAR) makes n = sign_extend(win) >> 8. There is no bounds check in win_UnlockWin.
g_8DA6 is unsigned char; decrement is one byte and wraps modulo 256. The zero check is on the post-decrement byte.
window count and i are signed 16-bit ints; the loop uses signed i < count and re-reads count each iteration.
Obj.type is plain char under the pinned MSC target, which is signed; the original loads one byte and sign-extends it before switch comparisons.
flags and each Rect field are 16-bit ints; masks are 16-bit constants.
pointer_arithmetic: win_handles[n]: far-pointer elements, 4-byte stride; registered base 55B3:9230.
g_8DA6[n]: byte stride; private BSS base 55B3:8DA6.
g_8CF2[n]: far-pointer elements, 4-byte stride; private BSS base 55B3:8CF2.
w->objs[i]: far object pointers, 4-byte stride from window offset +0x2C.
obj->h34 and obj->h2a: far handle-pointer fields at object offsets +0x34 and +0x2A; null is the pair of zero offset/segment words.
win_offsets[n]: Rect records of four words, 8-byte stride; registered base 50F6:4892.

The copied source address is the far pointer stored in w->objs[0], reinterpreted as far char*, plus 8 bytes; original code adds 8 to the offset word and keeps the segment word, then executes four MOVSW copies.
abi_and_pointer_conversions: Entry is _fastcall with 16-bit win in AX and a far return. The source parameter type and original use agree.
h is a 16:16 far pointer to a far master pointer. Casting it to struct Win far * far * preserves its 4-byte representation; the Ralloc Handle typedef is char far * far * with the same representation.
The source declares f_171C_2086 as void while its pinned implementation returns Handle. The target discards AX:DX, so the return-type declaration difference has no observable effect here.
f_171C_1686 returns a 16-bit int compared to 5; f_171C_13E4 and f_171C_20E2 return void. All are far calls with the 4-byte handle argument on the stack.

static_axes.finding: The enabled gate, both diagnostic paths and their continuation, byte decrement, nested-lock exit, three-part final-release gate, full object scan, type default, null-handle branch, both unlock outcomes, table clearing, map copy and far return all map to source lines 136-175 and the original sites in branch_map.

Every decoded conditional/loop site is listed. Signed type switch partitions 4/10 to h34, 16-18 to h2a, and all other signed-char values to continue. The count loop is signed and reevaluates count after each body.
All seven static call sites are listed. The source preserves the original order, conditional execution, 16:16 handle arguments and continuation after Punt if it returns.

All target-owned reads/writes are inventoried, including byte lock counter, flags/count, indexed far object and handle slots, helper-owned Ralloc writes, two cleared tables and the 8-byte Rect destination.
Masks, type values, field offsets, table lengths, 16-bit signed ints, unsigned-byte decrement, signed char promotion and signed loop test are accounted for.
All table strides, object-array stride, far-handle field offsets, Rect stride and byte +8 source calculation match the original indexed addressing and four-word copy.

Pinned m171C.c confirms the helper contracts: 1686 reads Ralloc type; 13E4 frees; 2086 decrements lock and returns an unused Handle; 20E2 sets type 3. Pointer representation and far-call arguments are compatible.

Child frees occur in ascending i order; each slot clears after its free; then window unlock, type update, win_handles clear, g_8CF2 clear, and Rect copy. Fallback performs only window unlock after the gate.
No source/original semantic difference was found on any decoded path under the pinned MSC 6.00AX 16-bit memory and ABI model; no codegen difference is needed to explain a semantic mismatch.

differential_evidence.limits: This is corroboration, not the static proof: the reviewed finite contract covers valid Ralloc-backed handles, depths 2/3/255, final-release flags 0/0x0200/0x0800/0x0A00, pending-update 0/1, 1-8 object trees, and object types {0,2,4,10,16,17,18,19}. Malformed handles/pointers, invalid Ralloc nodes and unsupported terminal heap paths are excluded.

review_notes: Static correspondence is conditional on the pinned MSC 6.00AX large-model ABI, signed plain-char behavior, and valid far pointers/layouts. win_UnlockWin has no explicit index bounds check; out-of-range n accesses remain outside the reviewed input domain.
The source and original both continue after either Punt call if Punt returns; this is represented in branch_map and call_map rather than assuming Punt is noreturn.
Differential evidence is finite and does not close malformed-handle or invalid-memory behavior. No such boundary was used to infer a missing branch or a semantic confirmation.
Original disassembly was obtained with tools/context.py win_UnlockWin without --raw. No raw byte array, byte capsule, production source edit, or generic matching search was used.

root_review.basis: Reviewed the whole-function branch/call/state/width maps, source/evidence identities, explanations of residue and differential/negative limits. Matching observed service boundaries are composed through the actual caller ABI and same callee/slot/state; finite coverage alone is not acceptance.
